summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma in remission and a history of recurrent cholangitis, was admitted with fever, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He was found to have E. coli bacteremia likely originating from the biliary tract, with imaging confirming persistent cholangitis and worsening biliary ductal dilation. Due to rising liver enzymes, he underwent an ERCP which revealed and cleared sludge and stone fragments from the bile ducts. He was treated with IV meropenem, and a PICC line was placed for continued outpatient antibiotic therapy. His pancytopenia, likely due to infection-related bone marrow suppression, was monitored without specific intervention. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with a two-week course of IV antibiotics, follow-up arranged with infectious disease and gastroenterology, and instructions to hold his probiotic until further guidance.
